content:
Title: Dashboards: incidents by status component + update timeliness + post-incident summary SLA

Context
This PR adds the dashboarding pieces for the Status Page Transparency Upgrades program. We’re getting repeated internal + support feedback that during incidents we’re missing:
- fast answers to “what’s impacted?” in a customer-comprehensible way (status_component)
- whether we’re meeting our external update cadence (time-to-first-update + overdue updates)
- whether we’re publishing post-incident summaries within the committed SLA

This PR is focused on dashboard panels and light query normalization. It intentionally does not change event emission (that’s in slo-toolkit/pr_88 and incident-bot PRs).

What’s included
1) New dashboard: “Status Transparency / Incident Comms”
- Incidents by status component (last 7d / 30d) as table + stacked timeseries
  - Grouping: status_component, severity, environment (hosted/dedicated/private), region
  - Filters: component, region, severity, incident_owner_team
- Update timeliness panels
  - Time to first public status update (p50/p90)
  - % incidents missing a first update within target window (by severity)
  - “Overdue next update” count (active incidents where next_update_at < now)
- Post-incident summary SLA panels
  - % Sev1+ incidents with customer summary published within 3 business days
  - Age distribution for missing summaries (bucketed)
  - Breakdown of SLA misses by status_component + owning team

2) Recording rules to make dashboard queries stable
We’ve seen drift in labels across sources (incident-bot vs manual updates). This PR adds a small set of recording rules that:
- coalesce component label keys into status_component
- backfill status_component="unknown" instead of dropping series
- normalize incident_id and incident_severity label formats

3) README notes for rollout
Adds a short “How to use / definitions” section so oncall + CS can interpret the charts consistently (e.g., what counts as a first update, what the SLA timer uses as ‘summary published’).

Data sources / assumptions
- Primary metrics expected by these panels:
  - incident_event_total{event="created|resolved|status_update_published|post_incident_summary_published", incident_id, incident_severity, status_component, region, environment}
  - incident_update_latency_seconds_bucket{kind="first_update", incident_severity, status_component}
  - incident_next_update_timestamp_seconds{incident_id} (gauge; emitted/updated by incident-bot)
- If incident_next_update_timestamp_seconds is absent (older incidents or bot disabled), the “overdue next update” panel will show as N/A for those incidents (documented in the dashboard notes).

Why this belongs in observability-pack
The observability-pack repo is where we keep shared dashboards + recording rules that ship to Hosted + Dedicated clusters. This dashboard is intended for:
- SRE oncall + incident commanders
- Support escalation liaison during incidents
- weekly reliability review (trend on which components are driving customer-visible incidents)

Screenshots (text description)
- Top row: KPI tiles for “Incidents (7d)”, “p90 time to first update”, “Overdue next updates”, “Summary SLA compliance (30d)”
- Middle: stacked bar by status_component for incident counts; timeseries with severity overlay
- Bottom: table of active incidents missing next_update_at, and table of incidents missing summaries with age

Implementation notes
- Business days: we’re not implementing true business-day math in PromQL. The SLA panel uses hours since resolved as a proxy, with a threshold of 72h. The dashboard includes an annotation: “SLA target: 3 business days; proxy threshold: 72h; review edge cases around holidays manually.” This mirrors what we agreed during planning and avoids embedding a timezone/calendar dependency here.
- Cardinality: grouping is capped via dashboard variables; default view is severity+component only. Region/environment/team breakdown is opt-in via variables to avoid accidentally expensive queries.

Files / areas changed
- dashboards/status_transparency/incident_comms_dashboard.jsonnet (new)
- dashboards/status_transparency/panels/incidents_by_component.libsonnet (new)
- dashboards/status_transparency/panels/update_timeliness.libsonnet (new)
- dashboards/status_transparency/panels/summary_sla.libsonnet (new)
- recording_rules/incident_comms_rules.yaml (new)
- recording_rules/README.md (updated)
- dashboards/README.md (updated with link + definitions)

Example query snippet (from dashboard)
- p90 time to first update (seconds):
  histogram_quantile(0.90, sum by (le, incident_severity) (rate(incident_update_latency_seconds_bucket{kind="first_update"}[30m])))

Commits
1. dashboards(status-transparency): add incident comms dashboard skeleton
2. panels: incidents by component (table + stacked) + variable wiring
3. panels: update timeliness (first update latency + overdue next update)
4. panels: post-incident summary SLA compliance + missing summary tables
5. rules: add incident comms recording rules + label normalization
6. docs: add dashboard usage notes + limitations

Testing / verification
- jsonnet compile: PASS
- dashboard lint (schema + variable references): PASS
- promtool rule check: PASS
- staging: validated panels populate for last week’s incidents in us-east (with known status_component coverage gaps noted as "unknown")

Rollout plan
- Merge behind existing dashboard sync pipeline.
- Deploy to SRE staging first, then production during next scheduled observability-pack sync.
- After incident-bot draft-sync rollout, re-check “overdue next updates” panel coverage (expected to improve).

Review conversation
Rafael Mendes (review) - 2024-06-27
- Can we add a panel that explicitly shows “% incidents missing a first update within target window by severity” rather than only latency percentiles? It’s what we’ll use for enforcement.

Allison Grant (author) - 2024-06-27
- Added panel “First update within target window” with thresholds: Sev0=10m, Sev1=15m, Sev2=30m (aligned with draft cadence doc). Uses a derived metric from first_update latency buckets.

Aisha Bello (review) - 2024-06-28
- Recording rule uses label_replace on incident_severity; can we make sure it doesn’t turn "sev1" into "Sev1" in some series and not others? We’ve had inconsistent casing.

Allison Grant (author) - 2024-06-28
- Good catch. Updated rule to normalize to lowercase internal label (incident_severity_norm=sev0|sev1|sev2|sev3) and the dashboard applies display mappings to show “Sev0/Sev1/...”. This keeps series stable.

Christine Wong (review) - 2024-06-30
- Request: rename "Capacity & Routing" variable to match status page taxonomy wording. Also can we pin the component variable order to the taxonomy list rather than alphabetic? It helps during incident comms.

Allison Grant (author) - 2024-06-30
- Renamed component display name to "Capacity & Routing" in legend mappings (data still uses status_component label). For ordering: Grafana variables don’t support explicit ordering from PromQL without an external list; added a dashboard note + suggested default filters. Happy to revisit if we want to hardcode options in jsonnet.

Chris Osei (review) - 2024-07-01
- The SLA compliance tile is “% within 72h”. Can we make the wording explicit so it doesn’t get quoted as a hard commitment? (We’re saying 3 business days externally.)

Allison Grant (author) - 2024-07-01
- Updated tile title to “Summary SLA (proxy: <72h)” and added a tooltip note. Also added an annotation row at top of dashboard with the business-day caveat.

CI / Checks
- build/jsonnet: PASS
- lint/dashboards: PASS
- promtool/rules: PASS
- e2e/render-dashboards: PASS

(Initial run failed on jsonnetfmt due to trailing whitespace in panels/update_timeliness.libsonnet; fixed in follow-up commit and reran.)

Merge
- Squash merged to main on 2024-07-02.

Follow-ups (not blocking)
- After incident-bot next_update_at enforcement lands, consider alerting on “overdue next update” for Sev0/Sev1 incidents.
- Once status_component tagging coverage reaches >95%, we can remove/quiet the “unknown component” warning banner.
